newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuclear plant finds new problem.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuclear plant finds new problem.

text.p: The troubled Maine Yankee nuclear power plant has found another potential problem with the system that would help cool the reactor in an accident, officials acknowledged Tuesday.

Maine Yankee notified the Nulear Regulatory Commission the feedwater line used to provide coolant to the reactor could be damaged if it suffered a break at the same time the plant lost off-site power.
"The probability of such an accident is very low, but the consequences could be significant," officials of the 25-year- old, 910-megwatt facility said in a statement.

The problem stems from a 1980s modification that switched an emergency feedwater pump from manual to automatic-start. The change could prevent the use of an alternative water supply that would keep the coolant line from breaking, officials said.

"It's similiar to the Three Mile Island (accident) where the emergency feedwater system was unavailable for several crucial minutes at the start of that accident due to some closed valves," David Lochbaum, a scientist at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told Maine Public Radio.

Maine Yankee spokeswoman Maureen Brown said officials did not know how much the problem would cost to correct. The problem must be repaired before the plant is allowed to restart, she and NRC officials said.

Officials said they have decided to inspect all of the 17,000 steam generator tubes resleeved two years ago because of cracking problems. Engineers expect only 0.5 percent to 1.0 percent of the tubes will need to be taken out of operation.
Maine Yankee has been off-line since December 6, 1996 to repair misrouted electrical cables. The plant is on the NRC's Watch List of troubled plants and will need the agency's approval to restart.

PECO Energy Co last week expressed an interest in buying in buying Maine Yankee from its current owners, Central Maine Power Co, New England Electric System, Northeast Utilities, and a group of other smaller New England utilities.
